subject.title: [Bug]: OpenAI-compatible streaming tool calls are dropped when provider omits finish_reason

question: Should OpenClaw treat native OpenAI-compatible `delta.tool_calls` followed by a clean raw SSE `[DONE]`, but no final `finish_reason`, as executable `toolUse`?
rationale: This changes a model-output-to-tool-execution boundary, and automation should not choose whether the clean-terminal signal is sufficient for shipped provider compatibility.

options.title: Accept clean-DONE tool execution
options.body: Land the transport-level fix after normal checks, using raw SSE `[DONE]` plus native tool-call deltas as the narrow no-finish execution contract.

options.title: Require exact provider proof first
options.body: Ask for one redacted Evolink or equivalent provider run before merge if maintainers want live proof from the originally reported route.

options.title: Keep finish_reason required
options.body: Leave the current fail-closed behavior in place and close or pause the candidate PR if maintainers decide explicit finish reasons are mandatory.

recommendation.title: Accept clean-DONE tool execution
recommendation.body: Land the transport-level fix after normal checks, using raw SSE `[DONE]` plus native tool-call deltas as the narrow no-finish execution contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored and merged adjacent tool-call terminal-safety work and are the strongest history signal for the execution-boundary decision.
